deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page continues a systematic table, begun on earlier pages, of primes p ≡ 1 (mod 8). For each prime it lists the classes of positive binary quadratic forms of determinant −p. Gauss writes forms as (a,b,c) = ax² + 2bxy + cy² with b² − ac = −p; the modern discriminant is −4p. In each case the class group is treated as cyclic, generated by g. 'Cl k.m' means the classes g^k and g^m = g^{−k}, which are inverse (opposite) classes; they are written together because they represent the same numbers. The header '{0,1,2,… / h, h−1, …}' sets up this pairing for class number h. 'c' (continet) gives a number represented by the class. A number in parentheses is the middle coefficient b of the form with that first coefficient. For classes of even index, i.e. the principal genus, Gauss also writes a decomposition of p into three squares.

Purpose of the three-square entries (art. 291–292 of the Disquisitiones). A representation p = A² + B² + C² gives a binary form of determinant −p: the form x²+y²+z² restricted to the lattice orthogonal to (A,B,C). Gauss finds a small number represented by that form and so identifies the class of the representation. Example for 929 = 22² + 21² + 2²: the vector (2,−2,−1) is orthogonal to (22,21,2) and has norm 9, so the class is g^6 = [3]^2, since 3 lies in class 3. The bookkeeping matches the count r3(p) = 12 h(−4p). There are h/2 principal-genus classes, merged in inverse pairs. Class 0 gets the representation with a zero, p = A² + B². The ambiguous class h/2, which contains the form (2,1,(p+1)/2), gets the representation with two equal squares. Each remaining pair gets one generic representation with 48 signed and ordered versions.

(1) End of p = 881 (h = 40; pairs k, 40−k):
- Cl 15.25: contains 30, via the form (30,13,35).
- Cl 16.24: 881 = 24² + 16² + 7²; contains 13. The orthogonal vector (2,−3,0) has norm 13.
- Cl 17.23: contains 23.
- Cl 18.22: 881 = 26² + 14² + 3²; contains 18. The orthogonal vector (1,−1,−4) has norm 18.
- Cl 19.21: contains 6.
- Cl 20: 881 = 9² + 20² + 20²; contains 2. This is the ambiguous class; the orthogonal vector (0,1,−1) has norm 2.
- These entries agree with [2] = g^20, [3] = g^1, [5] = g^6 and [13] = g^16. Checks: 6 lies in class 20±1 → 19; 18 = 2·9 lies in class 20±2 → 18; 30 = 2·3·5 lies in class 20+1−6 = 15.

(3) p = 937 (h = 20). Only the skeleton is written: Cl 0, 1.19, …, 6.14 in the left column, continued at the top right with 7.13, 8.12, 9.11, 10. Nothing is filled in.

(4) p = 953. The skeleton has h = 28 (pairs k, 28−k, with 14 self-inverse); nothing is filled in.

(5) p = 977 (h = 20). Skeleton only.

(6) Bottom table: all 38 primes p ≡ 1 (mod 8) below 1010, grouped by h(−4p).
- h = 4: 17, 73, 97, 193

All classes are checked mod 4, and mod 8 exactly when p = x² + 32y², with one exception: 953.
errors: p = 953 is wrongly given 28 classes, both in the section header {0/28} and in the bottom table. By my hand enumeration of reduced forms of discriminant −3812 the true count is h(−3812) = 32. This agrees with the criterion that 8 | h(−4p) iff p = x² + 32y², and 953 = 21² + 32·4². So the whole 953 skeleton has the wrong length. The crossed-out entry under 24 may reflect earlier hesitation about this prime.
929, Cl 0, 'c.11': 11 is not represented by any form of determinant −929, because −929 ≡ 6 is a non-residue mod 11. The principal class represents 1, so this is probably 'c.1' or a slip.

Not on this page but relevant: on the previous page, the entries for 881 'Cl 12 c:10' and 'Cl 11 c.30.7' seem inconsistent with [2] = g^20, [3] = g^1, [5] = g^6, which give 10 in class 14 and 30 in class 13 or 15. This may be a transcription problem.
Cl 12, Cl 14 and Cl 16 for 929 have their 'c' entries left blank. These are incomplete, not wrong.

results.what: Correspondence between the representations of a prime p ≡ 1 (mod 8) as a sum of three squares and the classes, paired with their inverses, of the principal genus of forms of determinant −p. Each class is placed in the cyclic class group via a small number represented by the orthogonal-lattice form.
results.modern_name: Gauss's theory of ternary/three-square representations (r3(p) = 12h(−4p)); the lattice orthogonal to a vector gives a binary form of discriminant −4p

results.what: Table of class numbers h(−4p) for all primes p ≡ 1 (mod 8) with p < 1010
results.modern_name: Class number tables for imaginary quadratic fields / forms x² + py²
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (extensive unpublished class-number tables); later Cayley and others

results.what: Explicit index in the cyclic class group of the classes containing small primes (e.g. for 929: [2] = g^18, [3] = g^3, [5] = g^2, [7] = g^11), checked by composition
results.modern_name: Discrete-log structure of the class group / composition of forms

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine numerical tables in the line of Disquisitiones art. 291–292 and Gauss's known class-number tables. The tabulated class numbers are consistent with the mod-8 regularity later proved by Barrucand–Cohn, but nothing on the page states that criterion. The one new fact is a computational error (h(−3812) is 32, not 28).

checkable.asserts: All three-square decompositions written for 929 are correct

checkable.sympy: len([(a,b,c) for a in range(32) for b in range(a+1) for c in range(b+1) if a*a+b*b+c*c==929]) == 10
checkable.asserts: 929 has exactly 10 essentially distinct three-square decompositions, matching the 10 principal-genus class pairs of h = 36

checkable.sympy: sum(1 for a in range(1,36) for b in range(-a+1,a+1) if b%2==0 and (b*b+3812)%(4*a)==0 and (b*b+3812)//(4*a)>=a and not (b<0 and (b*b+3812)//(4*a)==a)) == 32
checkable.asserts: h(−3812) = 32, so Gauss's value 28 for p = 953 is wrong

checkable.sympy: sum(1 for a in range(1,36) for b in range(-a+1,a+1) if b%2==0 and (b*b+3716)%(4*a)==0 and (b*b+3716)//(4*a)>=a and not (b<0 and (b*b+3716)//(4*a)==a)) == 36
checkable.asserts: h(−3716) = 36 for p = 929, as Gauss has it
11 is not represented by any form of determinant −929, so 'Cl 0 c.11' cannot be literal
(21,4,45) has determinant −929 and (30,13,35) has determinant −881; the parenthesised numbers are middle coefficients
The lattice orthogonal to (22,21,2) contains a vector of norm 9, matching 'c:9' for Cl 6
953 = x² + 32y², so 8 divides h(−4·953) and 28 is impossible
